chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Hamzah ibn al-Qasim al-Alavi al-Abbasi said: Ja'far ibn Malik al-Kufi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Hamid narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Abd al-Qudus narrated to us, saying: Al-A'mash, from Musa ibn Tarif, from Ubayyah ibn Rabi', said: Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) said:

I shall reason with the people on the Day of Resurrection with seven [things]: the establishment of prayer, the giving of alms-tax, enjoining good, forbidding evil, fair division with justice among the subjects, and the establishment of the prescribed limits.
ai.seo_question: What are the seven criteria Ali ibn Abi Talib uses to judge people on the Day of Resurrection?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Khisal*, Imam Ali (as) outlines seven criteria for divine evaluation, blending individual worship with communal governance. Notably, he includes 'fair distribution' (al-qism bi-l-sawi) and 'implementing limits' (iqamat al-hudud), highlighting the Shia emphasis on justice and leadership (Imamah) as integral to faith. This reflects the concept that political and social justice are not merely administrative duties but essential components of religious accountability.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 7-54 Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Hamzih ibn al-Qasim al-Alavi al-Ab’basi quoted Ja’far ibn Malik al-Kufy, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Hamid, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abdul Qoddoos, on the authority of Al-A’amash, on the authorityof Musa ibn Tarif, on the authority of Ababiat ibn Rub’ee Al-Asady that Ali ibn Abi Talib (MGB) said, “

On the Resurrection Day I shall reason with the people with the following seven things: establishment of prayers; payment of the alms-tax; enjoining to do good; admonishing against evil; just treatment of the people; fair division of the wealth; and being careful to carry out the decreed chastisements.”
